title: Report REST rate-limit from response headers, not the rate_limit endpoint, in protect.js
answers: protect workflow logs wrong rate limit remaining
why does the CI rate limit log always show 15000
how to read GitHub API remaining quota in a github-script workflow
body:
Symptom: The protection workflow's "Rate limit remaining" log showed a fixed 15,000 instead of the quota the workflow's own API calls were consuming.
Root cause: .github/workflows/protect.js:module.exports called github.rest.rateLimit.get() (the removed logRateLimit helper), which reports the nominal core allowance, not the budget charged by real requests.
Fix pattern: Register github.hook.after("request", ...) once at the top of the exported function and store response.headers["x-ratelimit-remaining"]; log that cached value once per polling cycle. Do not add standalone /rate_limit calls to measure quota.
Constraints: The value is undefined until the first real response, so the log is guarded by a !== undefined check. It reflects the latest request only, so it is logged after fetchChecks in the loop. Hooks are registered on the shared github instance, so keep a single registration per invocation.
applies: Applies to the GitHub-script workflow files under .github/workflows that use the injected github (Octokit) client and need to report quota.
says: Continuous integration logs show a stuck API rate limit instead of actual usage.
Branch protection check always reports fifteen thousand remaining quota in build output.
Display accurate remaining API budget in automated workflow polling logs.
Protection workflow run fails to reflect decreasing rate limits during status polling.
search: Workflows in .github/workflows/protect.js must extract remaining API quota from x-ratelimit-remaining response headers rather than querying the rate_limit endpoint. A github.hook.after request hook caches the header value, which is logged once per polling loop after fetchChecks if defined. Applies to github-script workflow files under .github/workflows that use the injected Octokit client and report quota without making standalone rate limit requests.
